steps.title: Source Control
steps.say: The editor has git built in. Let's make your first commit together: I'll point, you do it. The editor and terminal work normally while I'm here.

steps.title: One repository per folder
steps.say: Each numbered folder in this lesson is its own repository, so each one gets its own section here. Start with **01-first-commit**.

steps.title: Open the file
steps.say: Go to the **Explorer** (the top icon) and open `01-first-commit/roster.txt`.

steps.title: Make a change
steps.say: Add your name on a new line, then press **Ctrl+S** to save. The Source Control icon will show a number: that's how many files you've changed.

waitFor.hint: add your name and press Ctrl+S.

steps.title: Back to Source Control
steps.say: Open Source Control again to see your change.

steps.title: Your change
steps.say: There it is. **M** means modified. Click it to see exactly what changed, side by side.

steps.title: Stage it
steps.say: **Staging** picks what goes into the next commit. Hover over `roster.txt` and press the **+**.

steps.title: Commit it
steps.say: Type a message saying what you changed, like `Add my name to the roster`, then press **Commit**. A commit is a saved snapshot of your work.

waitFor.hint: write a message and press Commit.

steps.title: In the history
steps.say: Your commit is now at the top of the **Graph**: who made it, when, and your message.

steps.title: Which branch am I on?
steps.say: The bottom-left corner always shows your current branch. Click it to switch branches or make a new one. Our feature branches are named like `issue-12-add-turbo-boost`.

steps.title: The terminal
steps.say: Everything here can be done by typing git commands too.

steps.title: Try it
steps.say: Type `cd 01-first-commit`, press Enter, then `git log --oneline`. Your commit is the first line.

steps.title: Next exercises
steps.say: Each numbered folder's `README.md` has the next task: a feature branch, a merge, a conflict and a rebase. Check your progress in the lesson chip at the top.
